problem: Show that the variance-scaled normalized Turán deficit V*delta_D at the first-descent index D of a Poisson-binomial pmf with V >= 1 is bounded below by a universal constant (proved: 1/4), with the best constant shown to lie between 1/4 and 1/3.
debate: Quantitative strengthening of log-concavity for Bernoulli sums, in the line of Newton/Pitman, Darroch, Hillion-Johnson, Johnson, Dümbgen-Wellner and Bobkov-Marsiglietti-Melbourne (a literature of bounds, not a stated controversy).
gap: Known lower bounds on the Turán deficit delta_k depend on n or on the success probabilities and degenerate when near-0 and near-1 summands accumulate at fixed variance, while other results only locate the mode or bound mass ratios without controlling delta_k.
contribution: A variance-only bound V*delta_D >= 1/4 (hence f_{D+r}/f_D <= exp(-r/(4V))), a binomial family showing no constant above 1/3 works, and a proof combining known cubic and maximal-mass inequalities with an exact-arithmetic Bernstein-expansion check.
note: The problem and gap are crisp, but you never say why anyone needs a Turán deficit at the first descent specifically, so state in the first paragraph what a reader can do with the geometric tail bound that existing mode and ratio results do not already give.
